comparisons.title: 0580 Core and Extended calculator rounding-bound responses

dimensions.observation: Both cited covers permit a scientific calculator where appropriate; this common condition does not imply identical task operations.

P3/31 Q22(b), QP15, supplies the inequality symbols and asks two endpoints for a distance rounded to 97 km. P4/42 Q20, QP15, asks one lower volume bound from rounded mass 4810 g and density 7.7 g/cm³; the mass/density endpoints are unprompted intermediates. Two answer slots are therefore not evidence of greater demand than one.

P3 recovers a half-unit rounding interval, 96.5≤d<97.5. P4 rearranges the supplied density relation, selects the lower mass and upper density, and computes 4805/7.75=620 cm³. These are two reviewed source tasks, not a route-wide hierarchy.

MS31 p9 awards one mark for each endpoint in its correct position, with one special-case mark if both are reversed after zero. MS42 p10 awards three for 620 not from wrong working; its M2 and M1 alternatives recognise partial control of the quotient bounds. Neither scheme requires an invented universal chain.

uncertainties: Parent checked both rendered QPs and MS rows. This bounded comparison does not establish route-wide difficulty, calculator causality or syllabus exclusion.

comparisons.title: 0580 and 9709 Pure trigonometric equation demand

dimensions.observation: The sampled 0580 Extended non-calculator item states a degree interval. Within 9709 Pure, the P1 equation and P3 root sequence use radians, whereas the P2 phase-form item uses degrees. This sample therefore supports variation within 9709, not a blanket rule that 9709 questions use radians.
uncertainties: This is a bounded paper sample, not an exam-wide frequency claim.

dimensions.observation: The 0580 item begins directly with tan x = -1/sqrt(3); reference-angle/sign reasoning is a plausible route to its two interval answers. The sampled 9709 tasks vary: P1 converts a mixed-power equation into a quadratic in sin^2 theta or cos^2 theta; P2 creates R cos(theta-alpha), then explicitly reuses it in a Hence solution part; P3 supplies tan x = x + 2 as the target to prove from differentiation, then prompts graphical justification of given uniqueness, bracketing and iteration. The target equation is disclosed; its derivation is required. These are observed structures, not a universal difficulty ladder. Within P1, 9709/12 Q6 instead supplies an inverse-cosine equation already containing a quadratic in sin x: inverse-relation conversion replaces P1/11 Q4’s Pythagorean identity substitution. Both routes still require complete interval enumeration.

Neither the 0580 equation nor the 9709 P1/P2 phase-form item supplies a graph. P2 Q7 supplies y = 3 + sin^2(2x) - cos(2x), a labelled curve, dashed vertical boundaries at α and β and a shaded region; the limit values must be recovered. P3 Q6(b) instead prompts a suitable pair of sketches to justify the given only-one-root conclusion; y = tan x and y = x + 2 is the MS-supported choice, not a pair named in the QP. Diagram use varies with the sampled task.
uncertainties: No claim is made that diagrams occur in every P2 or P3 trigonometry question.

dimensions.observation: 0580/21 Q26 has substantial unruled working space followed by two answer blanks; its MS awards full credit for both correct answers, with alternative partial credits for one solution or a reference-angle observation. The sampled 9709/11 P1 item provides a full ruled page and awards identity substitution, quadratic solution and interval enumeration. P3 distributes work over four dependent parts: prove a supplied target equation, justify a supplied uniqueness conclusion using learner-selected sketches, bracket the root and record iterates. These are layouts and demands of the cited variants, not component-wide working-space rules. Within the same P1 component, variant 12 uses a separate answer booklet rather than variant 11’s ruled response page; Q6’s MS explicitly warns that final answers alone do not imply full marks.
uncertainties: 9709 P1/P2/P3 papers all allow calculators, while this particular 0580 item is Extended Paper 2 non-calculator; no causal claim about working space and calculator status is made.

dimensions.observation: The reviewed 0580 MS awards full three marks for both correct solutions; B2 for one correct answer OR B1 for a reference-angle observation are alternative partial credits, not a required/additive chain. The reviewed 9709 P1 MS credits identity conversion, a valid quadratic route and complete radian enumeration. The reviewed P3 MS credits a derivative, the pair y = tan x and y = x + 2 with justification, endpoint calculations and accuracy-justified iteration; degree-mode work earns no marks in parts (c)-(d). P1/12 Q6 credits inverse conversion, both sine values and three radian solutions; unlike the cited 0580 direct equation, its MS explicitly requires more than correct final answers alone. P2 Q4(b) credits use of their part (a) phase form and methods for both interval angles.
uncertainties: Method patterns are restricted to the listed reviewed schemes.

dimensions.observation: 0580/21 Q26 prints two x = slots requiring both solutions of one degree-valued unknown. 9709/11 Q4 asks to solve for one radian-valued theta without specifying a solution count; four solutions are derived, not four printed blanks. 9709/21 Q4(a) requests two distinct parameters (dimensionless R and degree-valued alpha), both required; (b) reuses them to solve for all interval values of theta on ruled lines without fixed answer slots. 9709/31 Q6(a-d) comprises four compulsory tasks about one root: supplied targets require proof/sketch justification, then a supplied bracket requires calculations and the final root requires recorded iterates. Printed subpart labels do not name extra unknowns or imply choice. P1/12 Q6 also leaves the solution count unstated: two intermediate sine values yield three radian x values, with no printed response slots.

Additional Pure items show varied transformations even within component: P2/21 Q2(a) solves a modulus equation and (b) reuses its roots as cotangent values, although the MS permits restarting. P3/31 Q5(a) proves a supplied reciprocal/double-angle identity and (b) explicitly reuses it to enumerate two radian solutions; degree answers receive a specific misread concession here, unlike the zero-credit degree-mode rule for Q6(c-d). These local marking differences must not become a universal radian-method rule.

uncertainties: The comparison covers selected 0580 Extended and 9709 Pure items only; it is not a Core-versus-AS/A or full-qualification comparison.
9709 A Level Pure scope includes P1 and P3, but full A Level qualification also has applied components outside this evidence project.

comparisons.title: Supplied information and response roles in stationary-point tasks

dimensions.observation: 0580/21 Q23 supplies a complete quadratic. 9709/12 Q5 supplies a second derivative and both coordinates of two minima, which constrain an unknown curve. 9709/21 Q7 supplies the full double-angle trigonometric curve plus a shaded-region sketch and names the two maximum x-values α and β. 9709/31 Q6(a) supplies an exponential/trigonometric curve, cos x ≠ 0 and the target stationary-point equation tan x = x + 2. The P3 target is given, so this evidence does not support a rule that later components always supply less.

0580/21 Q23 requests one coordinate pair in a printed two-coordinate template. 9709/12 Q5 also asks for one coordinate pair, but p and integration constants are intermediate unknowns. P2 Q7 asks for one exact area: maximum x-values are intermediate bounds, not separately requested final coordinates. P3 Q6(a) requests a derivation of the supplied equation, not stationary coordinates or a numerical root; later compulsory parts pursue the root.

0580/21 Q23 prints a quadratic and unruled working space with one coordinate-pair template. P1/12 Q5 prints a second derivative and minima without a graph, with responses in a separate answer booklet. P2/21 Q7 supplies a shaded curve and dashed vertical boundaries at α and β. P3/31 Q6(a) supplies symbolic data and ruled working lines without a curve plot. These are observations of these variants, not component-wide layout rules.

0580 syllabus p41 supports quadratic turning points by completing the square (E2.11) and elementary polynomial differentiation/stationary points (E2.12); the Q23 MS accepts multiple methods. P1 syllabus p22 supports integration constants and stationary points: Q5 integrates twice and uses supplied point conditions. P2 Q7 uses differentiation to derive integration bounds before finding an exact trigonometric area. P3 Q6(a) differentiates a composite exponential/trigonometric product, or uses the MS logarithmic route, and rearranges to the supplied equation. Shared stationarity does not make the surrounding operations equivalent.

0580 Q23 awards full marks for the coordinate pair with alternative partial routes. P1/12 Q5 makes all marks after the first stationarity-method mark dependent on using both given x-values in the integrated derivative with its constant; later marks credit second integration and point substitution. P2 Q7 credits derivative, maximum locations, integrand rewriting and exact definite integration. P3 Q6(a) credits derivative and valid derivation of the supplied equation, accepting product-rule or logarithmic differentiation routes. These are scheme-specific requirements, not a universal working ladder.

The sampled 0580 item is Extended non-calculator. The P1, P2 and P3 samples permit calculators, yet ask respectively for curve reconstruction, exact area and symbolic proof. Calculator permission alone does not describe the demanded response.

Within P1, /11 Q10(a) explicitly prescribes second-derivative classification of a supplied point; (b) asks for curve reconstruction; (c)(i) provides an optional factorisation identity for other stationary x-values; (c)(ii) asks their nature and the MS requires evaluated second derivatives. /12 Q5 instead combines second-derivative reconstruction and supplied minima into a single request for the other coordinate pair. syllabusRequirements.statement: P1 1.5 includes inverse-trigonometric principal-value notation and all solutions of simple trigonometric equations in a specified interval (syllabus p21).
P2 2.3 includes selecting identities for solving equations; its p24 detail explicitly includes R sin(theta ± alpha) and R cos(theta ± alpha) forms.

P3 products/quotients differentiation and numerical root-location/iteration objectives support the combined Q6 chain (syllabus pp28–29). These are P3 scope, not evidence that every trig task uses calculus.

9709-2-1-modulus-equations (syllabus PDF p23): understand the meaning of |x|, sketch the graph of y = |ax + b| and use relations such as |a| = |b| ⇔ a² = b² and |x − a| < b ⇔ a − b < x < a + b when solving equations and inequalities

9709-3-3-trig-functions (syllabus PDF p27): understand the relationship of the secant, cosecant and cotangent functions to cosine, sine and tangent, and use properties and graphs of all six trigonometric functions for angles of any magnitude

9709-3-3-trig-identities (syllabus PDF p27): use trigonometrical identities for the simplification and exact evaluation of expressions, and in the course of solving equations, and select an identity or identities appropriate to the context
9709-2-4-differentiation (syllabus PDF p24): use the derivatives of e^x, ln x, sin x, cos x, tan x, together with constant multiples, sums, differences and composites
9709-2-5-definite-integration (syllabus PDF p25): use trigonometrical relationships in carrying out integration

taskFamilies: Pure adds varied initial reductions and changes the role of a solution: an angle set, a supplied identity/proof target, an iterative root, or maxima used as area limits (9709-2026-mj-11-q4; 9709-2026-mj-12-q6; 9709-2026-mj-21-q2-b/q4-a/q4-b/q7; 9709-2026-mj-31-q5-a/q5-b/q6-a/q6-b/q6-c/q6-d). This is a demand comparison, not a proposal to put every task into one lab.
9709-2026-mj-11-q4: identity-led polynomial reduction and complete radian enumeration.
9709-2026-mj-12-q6: inverse-cosine relation to quadratic in sine, then three radian solutions.
9709-2026-mj-21-q4-a/b: determine two phase-form parameters, then use them for all interval angles.
9709-2026-mj-31-q6-a/b/c/d: prove supplied stationary-point equation, justify supplied uniqueness, prove supplied bracket, then iterate.

9709-2026-mj-21-q2-b: modulus-to-cotangent reuse; 9709-2026-mj-31-q5-a/q5-b: supplied reciprocal/double-angle identity proof followed by angle enumeration. 9709-2026-mj-21-q7: maxima determine limits for an exact area, a compound-task boundary.
givens: 9709-2026-mj-11-q4: 8 sin^4 theta - 6 cos^2 theta + 1 = 0, with 0 <= theta <= 2pi.

9709-2026-mj-12-q6: cos⁻¹(sin² x + (3/2)sin x) = (2/3)pi and 0 ≤ x ≤ 2pi are supplied. The inverse-cosine notation, quadratic expression inside it and radian interval are the complete symbolic stimulus.
9709-2026-mj-21-q4-a: 5 cos theta + 3 sin theta and the target R cos(theta - alpha), with R > 0 and 0 degrees < alpha < 90 degrees.
9709-2026-mj-21-q4-b: The equation 5 cos theta + 3 sin theta = 2 and open degree interval −180° < theta < 180°; Hence explicitly refers to the phase form from (a).
9709-2026-mj-31-q6-a: The curve y = e^(x^2 + 4x) cos^2 x, the restriction cos x != 0, and the required stationary-point equation tan x = x + 2.
9709-2026-mj-31-q6-b: The equation tan x = x + 2, the interval -pi < x < pi, and the conclusion that there is only one root are supplied.
9709-2026-mj-31-q6-c: The unique root from part (b) and endpoints 1.2 and 1.3.

9709-2026-mj-31-q6-d: The iterative formula x_(n+1) = tan^(-1)(x_n + 2), a root already bracketed in part (c), and output requirements of 3 decimal places with every iteration shown to 5 decimal places.
9709-2026-mj-21-q2-b gives |3cotθ+7|=|4cotθ−1|, 0<θ<π, with Hence referring to the algebraic roots of q2-a.
9709-2026-mj-31-q5-a supplies (cos x+sin x)(cosec x−sec x)≡2cot 2x to prove; q5-b sets the same product equal to 3 on 0≤x≤π.

9709-2026-mj-21-q7 gives y=3+sin²(2x)−cos(2x), 0≤x≤π, and a shaded sketch between maxima labelled α,β with dashed vertical boundaries to the x-axis. The maxima values are withheld, not their boundary roles.
requiredOutputs: P1/11 Q4 and P1/12 Q6 both ask for all solutions of one angle without specifying the count: four and three respectively are derived, not given slots.
P2/21 Q4(a) requests both exact R and degree-valued alpha to 2 d.p.; Q4(b) requests all theta values in an open degree interval.
P3/31 Q6(a-b) supplies conclusions to prove; (c) supplies bracket endpoints; (d) supplies the iteration and requires each iterate to 5 d.p. plus one final root to 3 d.p.

9709-2026-mj-21-q2-b requires both radian angles to 3 d.p. (greater accuracy allowed), without a printed count. 9709-2026-mj-31-q5-a requires a proof; q5-b requires all admissible angle values, with two solutions derived rather than a printed count.
9709-2026-mj-21-q7 asks an exact area, not two final angle values; α,β are intermediate integration limits.
outputForms: 9709-2026-mj-11-q4: ruled response page; 9709-2026-mj-12-q6: separate answer booklet, no QP working slots. Same component, different physical response format.
9709-2026-mj-21-q4-a/b: ruled working areas without fixed parameter/angle slots.
9709-2026-mj-31-q6-a/c/d: ruled proof/calculation areas; q6-b: unruled sketch space.
9709-2026-mj-21-q2-b and 9709-2026-mj-31-q5-a/q5-b have unlabelled ruled working space without fixed numerical slots. 9709-2026-mj-21-q7 requires an exact symbolic area.
explicitVariables: 9709-2026-mj-11-q4/12-q6 each use one radian angle. In 9709-2026-mj-21-q4-a, dimensionless R and degree phase α are outputs, then intermediates for θ in q4-b. 9709-2026-mj-31-q6 uses one radian root x and successive approximations x_n, not different unknown roots.
inferredVariables: 9709-2026-mj-11-q4 derives a squared trig value; 12-q6 derives two sine values; 21-q4-b selects offset-angle branches; 31-q6 requires a derivative, graph pair and endpoint evaluations. These intermediates are not automatically separate requested responses.
withheldInformation: 9709-2026-mj-12-q6 supplies neither conversion/quadratic steps nor solution count; 9709-2026-mj-31-q6-a supplies the target equation but withholds its derivation, and q6-b supplies uniqueness but withholds suitable sketches/justification.
representations: The selected P1 angle equations and P2 Q2(b)/Q4 are symbolic without supplied graphs (9709-2026-mj-11-q4; 9709-2026-mj-12-q6; 9709-2026-mj-21-q2-b/q4-a/q4-b). P2 Q7 instead supplies a shaded curve; P3 Q6(b) requires learner-selected sketches, with y=tan x and y=x+2 used by the MS.
dependencies: 9709-2026-mj-11-q4/12-q6 are standalone multistep equations. 9709-2026-mj-21-q4-b explicitly reuses the phase form from q4-a. 9709-2026-mj-31-q6-a–d concern the same equation/root with supplied targets; all four tasks are compulsory, not alternatives.

9709-2026-mj-21-q2-b says Hence, but MS10 expressly permits restarting instead of reusing q2-a. 9709-2026-mj-31-q5-b says Hence using the identity proved in q5-a. 9709-2026-mj-21-q7 derives maxima before evaluating the definite integral.
promptedWorking: 9709-2026-mj-31-q6 names proof, sketch, bracket and iteration tasks separately; 11-q4/12-q6 leave transformation and enumeration unpartitioned; 21-q4 separates phase-form construction from Hence solving.
implicitWorking: P1/12 Q6 leaves conversion and quadratic solving implicit; MS p15 expressly says correct final answers alone do not imply full marks. P2 Q4(b) leaves angle-branch selection implicit while its MS p12 credits methods for both.
workingDemands: The reviewed paired MS, not the size of a working area, establishes supported intermediate method/accuracy evidence. P1/12 Q6 credits conversion and both sine values before dependent enumeration credit; P3 Q6 assigns separate credit to its linked tasks.
markingDemands: 9709-2026-mj-12-q6 MS p15: all three radian solutions and no extras, with dependent credit and an explicit final-answers-alone limitation. 9709-2026-mj-21-q4-b MS p12: methods and accuracy for both interval angles using their phase form.

9709-2026-mj-21-q2-b MS10 allows degree working and restarting for M1 method credit; final A1 angle values remain radian values. 9709-2026-mj-31-q5-a MS13 permits expansion or a single-fraction route and working from both ends; full correct proof is required.

9709-2026-mj-31-q5-b MS14 permits solving 2cot2x=3 or tan²x+3tanx−1=0, ignores out-of-interval answers and applies a one-A1 degree-misread concession. This differs from 9709-2026-mj-31-q6-c/q6-d degree-mode zero-credit rules and must not become a universal trig marking rule.
9709-2026-mj-21-q7 MS15 contains dependent method marks for locating the maxima and using derived limits; merely displaying the two extrema does not meet the exact-area working demand.
supportedVariation: Within P1, different supplied algebraic representations demand different first transformations and produce different solution counts; neither prompt gives a blank per solution.

Units vary even within P2: 9709-2026-mj-21-q4 uses degrees, whereas q2-b and q7 use radian intervals. P3/31 Q6 supplies an equation, conclusion, bracket and iteration, so higher scope does not uniformly mean less supplied information.
boundaries: P1 is used in AS and A routes; P2 is AS-only; P3 is A Pure scope. These selected Pure components do not constitute the full A qualification.

The twelve mapped parts include proofs, numerical iteration and an area task; membership in a trig concept does not make each one a suitable periodic-angle lab task. The prerequisite 9709-2026-mj-21-q2-a is retrievable through q2-b but is not a trig-mapped provenance part.
counterexamples: P1/12 answer-booklet format contradicts any component-wide rule inferred from P1/11’s ruled page.
P3/31 Q6 discloses both target equation and uniqueness conclusion; those are not unknown results the learner is asked to guess.

9709-2026-mj-21-q2-b permits restarting despite Hence; 9709-2026-mj-31-q5-b permits an alternative quadratic route and a local degree-misread concession. 9709-2026-mj-21-q7 has a supplied shaded curve and an area output, unlike the symbolic angle tasks.
visualStructure: P1/12 Q6 is a compact equation and interval with a mark allocation but no response blanks. P1/11 Q4 occupies a ruled working page. P3/31 Q6(b) leaves unruled sketch space.
notation: P1/12 Q6 uses cos⁻¹ for the principal inverse relation, not a reciprocal. P3/31 Q6(d) uses indexed iterates x_n.
units: 9709-2026-mj-11-q4/12-q6 use radian intervals; 21-q4 uses degree θ/α and dimensionless R; 21-q2-b/q7 use radian intervals; 31-q5-b/q6 use radian values.
domainConventions: P1/12 Q6 asks for x in the closed interval from zero to 2pi; both derived sine values are admissible. P2/21 Q4(b) uses an open interval from −180 to 180 degrees.
intermediateQuantities: P1/12 Q6: the quadratic variable sin x takes two values, producing three x solutions. P2/21 Q4: R and alpha are final outputs of (a) but become intermediate parameters for (b).

designRecommendations: Design inference from 9709-2026-mj-11-q4/12-q6/21-q4-b/31-q5-b: a later transfer task could ask learners to identify the admissible branches after an algebraic reduction, keeping the first transformation and required final form source-specific. This is a benchmark, not approval to extend an existing degree-only lab across Pure.

Design inference from 9709-2026-mj-21-q7 and 9709-2026-mj-31-q6-a–d: retain calculus/area/proof/iteration as distinct compound demands; do not treat a visible angle solution as completion of their requested outputs.

syllabusRequirements.statement: 0580-c3-1 (syllabus PDF p20): Use and interpret Cartesian coordinates in two dimensions.
0580-c3-2 (syllabus PDF p20): Draw straight-line graphs for linear equations. Equations will be given in the form y = mx + c (e.g. y = –2x + 5), unless a table of values is given.
0580-c3-3 (syllabus PDF p20): Find the gradient of a straight line. From a grid only.

0580-c3-5 (syllabus PDF p20): Interpret and obtain the equation of a straight-line graph in the form y = mx + c.
Questions may:
 • use and request lines in the forms 
y = mx + c  
x = k
 • involve finding the equation when the graph is given
 • ask for the gradient or y-intercept of a graph from an equation, e.g. find the gradient and y-intercept of the graph with the equation  
y = 6x + 3. 
Candidates are expected to give equations of a line in a fully simplified form.

0580-c3-6 (syllabus PDF p20): Find the gradient and equation of a straight line parallel to a given line.
e.g. find the equation of the line parallel to 
y = 4x – 1 that passes through (1, –3).

0580-e3-3 (syllabus PDF p43): 1 Find the gradient of a straight line.
2  Calculate the gradient of a straight line from the coordinates of two points on it.

0580-e3-5 (syllabus PDF p43): Interpret and obtain the equation of a straight-line graph.
Questions may:
 • use and request lines in different forms, e.g. 
ax + by = c 
y = mx + c 
x = k
 • involve finding the equation when the graph is given
 • ask for the gradient or y-intercept of a graph from an equation, e.g. find the gradient and y-intercept of the graph with equation  
5x + 4y = 8.
Candidates are expected to give equations of a line in a fully simplified form.

taskFamilies: The sampled line family changes which representation is supplied and which must be produced: point reading/plotting, line drawing, graph-to-equation and equation/point-to-parallel-line (0580-2025-on-13-q5-a/q5-d; 0580-2025-on-32-q4-a/q4-b/q4-c; 0580-2025-on-31-q21; 0580-2025-on-32-q25-a/q25-b; 0580-2025-on-33-q26; 0580-2025-on-41-q17).

Recover an equation from a supplied graph: 0580-2025-on-31-q21, 0580-2025-on-32-q25-a and 0580-2025-on-33-q26. Construct a parallel line from equation/point data: 0580-2025-on-32-q25-b. Construct from two coordinates: 0580-2025-on-41-q17.
givens: 0580-2025-on-13-q5-a/q5-d share a quadrilateral on a 1 cm² Cartesian grid, with A(−2,−2), B(−1,2), C(2,2), D(3,−2) plotted; q5-d supplies E=(−3,2). The plotted vertices are a visual stimulus, not four requested coordinate outputs.
0580-2025-on-32-q4-a/q4-b/q4-c share axes −4 to 4 and plotted P=(−2,3); q4-b supplies y=x; q4-c requests a perpendicular through P.

Coefficients are read/derived, not printed parameters.

0580-2025-on-32-q4-b/q4-c each require a drawn line; no equation is requested for q4-c. Each graph/equation task 0580-2025-on-31-q21, 0580-2025-on-32-q25-a/q25-b, 0580-2025-on-33-q26 and 0580-2025-on-41-q17 has one y= blank.

0580-e6-3 (syllabus PDF p51): Know the exact values of:
1 sin x and cos x for x = 0°, 30°, 45°, 60° and 90°.
2 tan x for x = 0°, 30°, 45° and 60°.

0580-e6-4 (syllabus PDF p51): 1 Recognise, sketch and interpret the following graphs for 0° ≤ x ≤ 360°:
• y = sin x
• y = cos x
• y = tan x.
2 Solve trigonometric equations involving sin x, cos x or tan x, for 0° ≤ x ≤ 360°.
e.g. solve:
• sin x = 2/3 for 0° ≤ x ≤ 360°
• 2 cos x + 1 = 0 for 0° ≤ x ≤ 360°.

taskFamilies: A full-cycle sketch, all roots on a full interval and one reflex-domain root are distinct completion criteria within the same non-calculator component (0580-2025-on-22-q21-a; 0580-2025-on-23-q17-a; 0580-2025-on-21-q26; 0580-2025-on-22-q21-b; 0580-2025-on-23-q17-b).

0580-2025-on-22-q21-a and 0580-2025-on-23-q17-a request a full cosine sketch; 0580-2025-on-21-q26 and 0580-2025-on-22-q21-b request both degree roots; 0580-2025-on-23-q17-b restricts the answer to a reflex angle.
givens: 0580-2025-on-21-q26: tan x=−1/√3, 0°≤x≤360°, with no reference angle, graph or quadrant cue.
0580-2025-on-22-q21-a and 0580-2025-on-23-q17-a: y=cos x on supplied axes 0°≤x≤360°, with ordinate scale −1 to 1; the curve is withheld.
explicitVariables: x is one degree angle in the three solving parts (0580-2025-on-21-q26; 0580-2025-on-22-q21-b; 0580-2025-on-23-q17-b); y is the cosine ordinate in the two sketch parts. Multiple x= blanks do not denote distinct variables.
inferredVariables: 0580-2025-on-21-q26 and 0580-2025-on-22-q21-b use a 30° reference angle with different sign/period constraints; 0580-2025-on-23-q17-b uses 45° and the reflex restriction. These angles are not supplied.
requiredOutputs: 0580-2025-on-21-q26 requires both degree solutions in two x= blanks; 0580-2025-on-22-q21-b also requires both, with blanks joined by “or”. 0580-2025-on-23-q17-b requires only the one solution satisfying the reflex constraint.
0580-2025-on-22-q21-a and 0580-2025-on-23-q17-a require a curve through (0,1),(180,−1),(360,1), not numerical answer slots.
visualStructure: 0580-2025-on-21-q26 has substantial unruled space and two answer blanks. 0580-2025-on-22-q21-a/23-q17-a have axes but no supplied cosine curve; their solving subparts do not explicitly require a graphical solution.
units: All five cited tasks are degree-based non-calculator P2 tasks; ordinate values in the sketches are cosine values (0580-2025-on-22-q21-a; 0580-2025-on-23-q17-a).
dependencies: 0580-2025-on-22-q21-b uses the same cosine function as q21-a, but a graphical solution is not explicitly required. The reflex restriction is supplied directly in 0580-2025-on-23-q17-b; an earlier drawn curve is not claimed as a mandatory method.
markingDemands: 0580-2025-on-21-q26 MS10 awards full 3 for both answers; B2 for one or B1 for a ±30° inverse value are alternatives, not additive stages.

0580-2025-on-22-q21-b MS11 awards 3 for both roots, with partial credits for one root, isolated cosine or reference angle and a source-specific special case. 0580-2025-on-23-q17-b MS7 awards 2 for 315°, with B1 for 45°.
0580-2025-on-22-q21-a MS11 and 0580-2025-on-23-q17-a MS7 award 2 for the cosine sketch; M1 permits the stated almost-correct shape/endpoint/curvature cases.
supportedVariation: 0580-2025-on-22-q21-b versus 0580-2025-on-23-q17-b changes the requested domain from a full cycle to reflex angles, changing the admissible output set. This is not simply a two-blank versus one-blank difficulty contrast.
boundaries: Five mapped parts from three O/N2025 Extended P2 variants only; no Core or P4 equation/sketch claim is inferred from their absence in this concept-link sample.
counterexamples: 0580-2025-on-23-q17-b deliberately has one admissible solution; “always two roots” would be false. 0580-2025-on-22-q21-a and 0580-2025-on-23-q17-a provide axes, not a graph to read.

designRecommendations: Design inference from 0580-2025-on-21-q26, 0580-2025-on-22-q21-b and 0580-2025-on-23-q17-b: require the learner to select the complete admissible set and test it against sign, period and interval. Change the domain as well as the equation; do not reveal a root by moving a model alone.

Design inference from 0580-2025-on-22-q21-a/23-q17-a: connect learner sketch choices to visible cosine values while keeping sketch production distinct from equation solving. Treat this as a comparison benchmark pending live-lab feasibility review.

(a) linear
(b) quadratic
(c) cubic
(d) reciprocal
(e) exponential.
Functions will be equivalent to:
• ax + by = c
• y = ax² + bx + c
• y = ax³ + b
• y = ax³ + bx² + cx
• y = a/x + b
• y = arˣ + b
where a, b and c are rational numbers and r is a rational, positive number.
Knowledge of turning points, roots and symmetry is required.
Knowledge of vertical and horizontal asymptotes is required.
Finding turning points of quadratics by completing the square is required.

0580-e2-12 (syllabus PDF p41): 1 Estimate gradients of curves by drawing tangents.
2 Use the derivatives of functions of the form axⁿ, where a is a rational constant and n is a positive integer or zero, and simple sums of not more than three of these.
3 Apply differentiation to gradients and stationary points (turning points).
4 Discriminate between maxima and minima by any method.
dy/dx notation will be expected.
Maximum and minimum points may be identified by:
• an accurate sketch
• use of the second differential
• inspecting the gradient either side of a turning point.
Candidates are not expected to identify points of inflection.
0580-c1-6 (syllabus PDF p14): Use the four operations for calculations with integers, fractions and decimals, including correct ordering of operations and use of brackets.

0580-e1-12 (syllabus PDF p35): 1 Use common measures of rate.
2 Apply other measures of rate.
3 Solve problems involving average speed.

taskFamilies: The output role changes from an expression or symbolic rearrangement to numerical solutions, a constraint-derived parameter, or proof of a supplied equation; these are not interchangeable solve-for-x tasks (0580-2025-on-11-q29; 0580-2025-on-21-q17-b; 0580-2025-on-22-q22; 0580-2025-on-41-q24-b; 0580-2025-on-41-q26).
givens: Angle expressions on a parallelogram provide a geometric equation constraint; dollar payment with cent prices requires a consistent monetary unit; the supplied monic completed-square form fixes scale that a minimum point alone would not determine (0580-2025-on-12-q12-a; 0580-2025-on-22-q8; 0580-2025-on-23-q14-b).
requiredOutputs: Three coefficients belong to one identity, four coordinate blanks encode two paired solutions, two x blanks require both quadratic roots, and h/min blanks encode one duration. In the three-equal-expressions task, x is an intermediate for the requested y (0580-2025-on-21-q18; 0580-2025-on-23-q27; 0580-2025-on-41-q24-c; 0580-2025-on-41-q24-d; 0580-2025-on-43-q14).

The supplied journey target needs error-free derivation, while rearrangement credits denominator clearing, collection and factor/division with follow-through; do not treat final blanks as the complete working demand (0580-2025-on-11-q29; 0580-2025-on-21-q8; 0580-2025-on-41-q24-b; 0580-2025-on-43-q17).

syllabusRequirements.statement:
0580-e2-6 (syllabus PDF p39): 1 Represent and interpret inequalities, including on a number line.
2 Construct, solve and interpret linear inequalities.
3 Represent and interpret linear inequalities in two variables graphically.
4 List inequalities that define a given region.
The following conventions should be used:
• broken lines should be used to represent strict inequalities (<, >)
• solid lines should be used to represent inclusive inequalities (⩽, ⩾)
• shading should be used to represent unwanted regions (unless otherwise directed in the question).
Linear programming problems are not included.

taskFamilies: The direction of translation reverses: a two-dimensional region becomes simultaneous inequalities, while a supplied inequality becomes a one-dimensional drawing (0580-2025-on-21-q16; 0580-2025-on-22-q7).
givens: The region uses vertical, horizontal and sloping graph boundaries; the number-line task supplies −4<x≤3, so its endpoint values are not to be solved (0580-2025-on-21-q16; 0580-2025-on-22-q7).
requiredOutputs: Four written inequalities jointly define one region, not four alternatives. One interval drawing must distinguish the open and closed endpoints (0580-2025-on-21-q16; 0580-2025-on-22-q7).

0580-e5-3 (syllabus PDF p49): 1  Carry out calculations involving the circumference and area of a circle.
2  Carry out calculations involving arc length and sector area as fractions of the circumference and area of a circle.
Answers may be asked for in terms of π.
Formulas are given in the List of formulas.
Includes minor and major sectors.

taskFamilies: Sector fraction may be inferred from perimeter, supplied for a proof target, or switched between a minor area and major arc (0580-2025-on-21-q12; 0580-2025-on-22-q23-a; 0580-2025-on-23-q19-a; 0580-2025-on-23-q19-b).
givens: The first task supplies radius and perimeter rather than angle; the second supplies a major-sector angle and arc target; the third retains the minor angle while asking the complementary major arc (0580-2025-on-21-q12; 0580-2025-on-22-q23-a; 0580-2025-on-23-q19-b).
requiredOutputs: An exact area in cm², derivation of an already supplied arc and exact arc length in cm are different final roles (0580-2025-on-21-q12; 0580-2025-on-22-q23-a; 0580-2025-on-23-q19-b).
markingDemands: The MS recognises either the derived angle/fraction or a perimeter equation as intermediate progress; no single angle-first route is mandatory (0580-2025-on-21-q12).

2 Recognise patterns in sequences, including the term-to-term rule, and relationships between different sequences.

taskFamilies: Next value, term-to-term rule, membership decision and nth-term expression test different uses of a sequence; a table of three formulas does not mean three unknown positions (0580-2025-on-11-q7-a; 0580-2025-on-11-q7-b; 0580-2025-on-13-q21-c-ii; 0580-2025-on-23-q16).
givens: An explicit nth term supplies the rule in some tasks, while others give terms with arithmetic, fractional or geometric structure. A decreasing formula supplies a greatest-term question rather than a request for its index (0580-2025-on-12-q27-b; 0580-2025-on-23-q16; 0580-2025-on-43-q1-b).
dependencies: Testing the proposed term uses the prior nth-term expression and the requirement that positions are positive integers; a real solution for n is insufficient (0580-2025-on-13-q21-c-ii).
markingDemands: The MS credits the equation and a supported non-membership reason separately, with stated follow-through on a suitable earlier linear rule (0580-2025-on-13-q21-c-ii).

syllabusRequirements.statement:
0580-e4-4 (syllabus PDF p47): 1 Calculate lengths of similar shapes.
2 Use the relationships between lengths and areas of similar shapes and lengths, surface areas and volumes of similar solids.
3 Solve problems and give simple explanations involving similarity.
Includes use of scale factor, e.g. Volume of B / Volume of A = (Length of B / Length of A)³.
Includes showing that two triangles are similar using geometric reasons.

0580-e4-6 (syllabus PDF p48): 1 Calculate unknown angles and give simple explanations using the following geometrical properties:
• sum of angles at a point = 360°
• sum of angles at a point on a straight line = 180°
• vertically opposite angles are equal
• angle sum of a triangle = 180° and angle sum of a quadrilateral = 360°.
2 Calculate unknown angles and give geometric explanations for angles formed within parallel lines:
• corresponding angles are equal
• alternate angles are equal
• co-interior angles sum to 180° (supplementary).
3 Know and use angle properties of regular and irregular polygons.
Knowledge of 3-letter notation for angles is required, e.g. angle ABC. Candidates are expected to use the correct geometrical terminology when giving reasons for answers.
Includes exterior and interior angles, and angle sum.
0580-c4-4 (syllabus PDF p23): Calculate lengths of similar shapes.

taskFamilies: Similarity can be a supplied relation, a proof target or an intermediate scale law linking length, area and capacity (0580-2025-on-21-q14-b-ii; 0580-2025-on-22-q11-a; 0580-2025-on-22-q11-c; 0580-2025-on-43-q22-b).
givens: Parallel sides support the nested-triangle proof; matching side roles identify a linear scale; similar containers supply surface areas and one capacity without a concrete shape diagram (0580-2025-on-22-q11-a; 0580-2025-on-33-q29-a; 0580-2025-on-43-q22-b).
requiredOutputs: Two ratio blanks encode one ordered area ratio. The quadrilateral asks an area expression in k after subtracting the inner triangle; capacity requires recovering a linear scale from areas before applying its cube (0580-2025-on-21-q14-b-ii; 0580-2025-on-22-q11-c; 0580-2025-on-43-q22-b).
counterexamples: No actual container shape or dimensions are supplied, so deriving a particular cylinder or prism formula would be invented modelling (0580-2025-on-43-q22-b).

syllabusRequirements.statement:
0580-e5-4 (syllabus PDF p49): Carry out calculations and solve problems involving the surface area and volume of a:
 • cuboid
 • prism
 • cylinder
 • sphere
 • pyramid
 • cone.
Answers may be asked for in terms of π.
The following formulas are given in the List of formulas:
 • curved surface area of a cylinder
 • curved surface area of a cone
 • surface area of a sphere
 • volume of a prism
 • volume of a pyramid
 • volume of a cylinder
 • volume of a cone
 • volume of a sphere.
The term prism refers to any solid with a uniform cross-section, e.g. a cylindrical sector.

0580-e6-2 (syllabus PDF p51): 1 Know and use the sine, cosine and tangent ratios for acute angles in calculations involving sides and angles of a right-angled triangle.
2 Solve problems in two dimensions using Pythagoras’ theorem and trigonometry.
3 Know that the perpendicular distance from a point to a line is the shortest distance to the line.
4 Carry out calculations involving angles of elevation and depression.
Angles will be given in degrees and answers should be written in degrees, with decimals correct to one decimal place.
Knowledge of bearings may be required.

0580-e5-5 (syllabus PDF p50): 1  Carry out calculations and solve problems involving perimeters and areas of:
• compound shapes
• parts of shapes.
2  Carry out calculations and solve problems involving surface areas and volumes of:
• compound solids
• parts of solids.
Answers may be asked for in terms of π.
e.g. find the surface area and volume of a frustum.

0580-e2-5 (syllabus PDF p38): 1 Construct expressions, equations and formulas.
2 Solve linear equations in one unknown.
3 Solve fractional equations with numerical and linear algebraic denominators.
4 Solve simultaneous linear equations in two unknowns.
5 Solve simultaneous equations, involving one linear and one non-linear.
6 Solve quadratic equations by factorisation, completing the square and by use of the quadratic formula.
7 Change the subject of formulas.

0580-c5-4 (syllabus PDF p25): Carry out calculations and solve problems involving the surface area and volume of a:
 • cuboid
 • prism
 • cylinder
 • sphere
 • pyramid
 • cone.
Answers may be asked for in terms of π.
The following formulas are given in the List of formulas:
 • curved surface area of a cylinder
 • curved surface area of a cone
 • surface area of a sphere
 • volume of a prism
 • volume of a pyramid
 • volume of a cylinder
 • volume of a cone
 • volume of a sphere.
The term prism refers to any solid with a uniform cross-section, e.g. a cylindrical sector.

0580-c1-3 (syllabus PDF p13): Calculate with the following:
• squares
• square roots
• cubes
• cube roots
• other powers and roots of numbers.

0580-e1-13 (syllabus PDF p35): 1 Calculate a given percentage of a quantity.
2 Express one quantity as a percentage of another.
3 Calculate percentage increase or decrease.
4 Calculate with simple and compound interest.
5 Calculate using reverse percentages.
Problems may include repeated percentage change.

taskFamilies: Supplied surface area can determine length, equal volumes can constrain a new solid, and a volume-preserving remelt can end in surface area; the requested invariant must be identified (0580-2025-on-31-q13-a; 0580-2025-on-32-q19; 0580-2025-on-41-q14-d; 0580-2025-on-23-q29).
givens: Rolling the given sector fixes the cone’s slant height and circumference relation. A sphere touching cube faces has its exact volume supplied as a show-that target. Composite solid drawings distinguish exposed surfaces from internal joins (0580-2025-on-22-q23-b; 0580-2025-on-41-q14-a; 0580-2025-on-23-q29).
requiredOutputs: A prescribed exact cone volume is one expression, not separate a,b blanks; equal total areas ask R in terms of x, not a numerical radius; remelting asks cylinder surface area after deriving height (0580-2025-on-22-q23-b; 0580-2025-on-23-q29; 0580-2025-on-41-q14-d).
dependencies: The supplied sphere volume supports both an unoccupied-cube percentage and the cylinder’s volume constraint; copying the provided volume does not complete either later output (0580-2025-on-41-q14-b; 0580-2025-on-41-q14-d).

syllabusRequirements.statement:
0580-e2-11 (syllabus PDF p41): Recognise, sketch and interpret graphs of the following functions:
(a) linear
(b) quadratic
(c) cubic
(d) reciprocal
(e) exponential.
Functions will be equivalent to:
• ax + by = c
• y = ax² + bx + c
• y = ax³ + b
• y = ax³ + bx² + cx
• y = a/x + b
• y = arˣ + b
where a, b and c are rational numbers and r is a rational, positive number.
Knowledge of turning points, roots and symmetry is required.
Knowledge of vertical and horizontal asymptotes is required.
Finding turning points of quadratics by completing the square is required.

0580-e2-12 (syllabus PDF p41): 1 Estimate gradients of curves by drawing tangents.
2 Use the derivatives of functions of the form axⁿ, where a is a rational constant and n is a positive integer or zero, and simple sums of not more than three of these.
3 Apply differentiation to gradients and stationary points (turning points).
4 Discriminate between maxima and minima by any method.
dy/dx notation will be expected.
Maximum and minimum points may be identified by:
• an accurate sketch
• use of the second differential
• inspecting the gradient either side of a turning point.
Candidates are not expected to identify points of inflection.

taskFamilies: The supplied explicit quadratic asks for one turning-point coordinate pair; classification as a maximum is not a separately requested response (0580-2025-on-21-q23).
givens: The equation is given, with unruled working space and a single coordinate-pair template; both x and y are withheld (0580-2025-on-21-q23).
markingDemands: The MS awards full credit for the pair and has alternative derivative, vertex-formula and completing-square partial routes. These OR branches are not additive or a mandatory method chain (0580-2025-on-21-q23).

taskFamilies: The sample moves between constructing displays, proving supplied summary targets, comparing supplied variability and criticising misleading visual scales (0580-2025-on-11-q14-a; 0580-2025-on-11-q14-c; 0580-2025-on-32-q20-b; 0580-2025-on-33-q7).

requiredOutputs: A supplied median requires demonstration. Two missing sectors, three angle-table cells and a whole chart from one radius are different graphical completion roles; the two patient blanks identify two distinct ordered quantities (0580-2025-on-11-q14-c; 0580-2025-on-31-q12-b; 0580-2025-on-32-q12-a; 0580-2025-on-32-q12-b; 0580-2025-on-42-q6).
dependencies: The changed-median decision uses the enlarged dataset, not only the old value; a new innings score is recovered by comparing totals derived from two means and sample sizes (0580-2025-on-12-q11-d-ii; 0580-2025-on-33-q10-b).
markingDemands: A direction-only median response lacks the required reason. Pie-chart follow-through permits the stated drawing from earlier angles; it does not make tabulated angles alone a completed chart (0580-2025-on-12-q11-d-ii; 0580-2025-on-32-q12-b).

0580-c7-1 (syllabus PDF p28): Recognise, describe and draw the following transformations:
1 Reflection of a shape in a vertical or horizontal line.
2 Rotation of a shape about the origin, vertices or midpoints of edges of the shape, through multiples of 90°.
3 Enlargement of a shape from a centre by a scale factor.
4 Translation of a shape by a column vector (x, y).
Questions will not involve combinations of transformations. A ruler must be used for all straight edges.
Positive and fractional scale factors only.

0580-e7-1 (syllabus PDF p53): Recognise, describe and draw the following transformations:
1 Reflection of a shape in a straight line.
2 Rotation of a shape about a centre through multiples of 90°.

4 Translation of a shape by a column vector (x, y).
Questions may involve combinations of transformations. A ruler must be used for all straight edges.
Positive, fractional and negative scale factors may be used.
